name: Tone Mapping Analysis
description: Analyzes HDR tone mapping artifacts to detect synthetic artifacts, anomalies, and characteristic signatures of generative AI models.
algorithm: Tone Mapping Analysis — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes tone mapping characteristics for image forensic analysis:

1. **Tone Curve Estimation**: The effective tone curve (mapping from scene luminance to pixel values) is estimated from the image content. This is done by analyzing: highlight rolloff behavior, shadow detail rendering, and the overall luminance distribution relative to expected scene statistics.

2. **Tone Mapping Operator Detection**: Different cameras and processing pipelines apply different tone mapping operators (TMOs). The method identifies the TMO type — standard curves (sRGB gamma), camera-specific tone curves (S-curves), HDR tone mapping (Reinhard, Drago, Mantiuk), or AI-generated tone mapping. AI generators learn tone mapping from their training data and may produce inconsistent or unusual tone curves.

3. **Per-Region Tone Response Analysis**: The local tone response is analyzed in different image regions. In single-capture images, the same tone curve applies globally. Composite images may show different effective tone curves in different regions — a key indicator of manipulation.

4. **Dynamic Range Consistency**: The effective dynamic range and its distribution across the image are analyzed. Natural single-capture images have consistent dynamic range limited by the sensor. AI-generated images may show dynamic range inconsistencies — regions with impossible dynamic range extension or unnatural highlight-shadow balance.

5. **Tone Mapping Forensic Score**: Tone mapping features (estimated TMO parameters, per-region tone response consistency, dynamic range analysis) are combined into a forensic score. The score captures tone mapping inconsistencies indicative of compositing, AI generation, or post-processing manipulation.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: image
Input: Raw pixel data / image file
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Processing: Client-side Canvas API
Color spaces: RGB, Grayscale as applicable
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-90% standalone accuracy. Performance is highest on uncompressed images and may decrease with heavy JPEG compression or social media re-encoding.
source: Digital image forensics research. Based on signal processing and computational photography principles.
useCase: Detection of AI-generated or manipulated images through tone mapping analysis analysis. This method identifies patterns and artifacts that are characteristic of AI generation, contributing to a comprehensive image forensic analysis.
strengths:
• Fast client-side processing using Canvas API
• Effective at detecting specific AI generation artifacts
• Works with common image formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP)
• Can be combined with complementary analysis methods
• Based on established image forensics research
limitations:
• Performance may vary with image compression level
• Social media re-encoding can affect accuracy
• Best used in combination with other forensic methods
• May produce false positives on heavily processed authentic images
• Effectiveness depends on the AI generation model used
